why: Causal reasoning about what uneven allocation does to a team; the excluded statement is recognisably about a different subject.
'Optimal' implies trade-off across several factors, so the single-factor and punitive options fail on their own terms.
Reasoning about which tier does day-to-day people work, but the item is genuinely ambiguous — the guide assigns Manage Project Team to the project manager, as the bank's own note concedes.
Recognising commercial product names; no amount of resource-management understanding tells you which vendors exist.
Follows from what distance does to communication; the other options are advantages, wrong on their face.
Negative form over the guide's named examples of networking; the odd one out is off-list rather than logically inconsistent.
Reasoning from geographic dispersion to what it most threatens, though team-building is a defensible competing read.
A practitioner could reasonably answer 'the project manager'; only the guide's explicit statement fixes shared enforcement.
Turns on which word pairs with 'retention' to cover the whole employment cycle — a language judgement, not a recalled fact.
Maps a situation onto a named HR technique with no derivation path, and the bank flags its own answer as uncertain outside PMBOK terminology.
